                 Dr Lisa Smith
                 Endocrinologist
                 City Hospital
                 Newtown

                 10/02/2014

                 Dear Dr Smith
                 Re: Mrs Priya Sharma DOB:08/05/1953

                 Thank you for seeing Mrs Sharma, who has been presented with uncontrolled blood sugar levels. Your further management would
                 be valued.

                 Mrs Sharma has had NIDDM since 1994. She takes metformin, 500mg two tablets at night and glipizide, 5mg two tablets in the
                 morning. Her family history is notable for type 2 diabetes related to her relatives, no history of formal exercise.

                 On 29/12/2013, Mrs Sharma came to my clinic concerned regarding her glucose levels are not properly enough regulated. Her
                 assessment showed BMI 24 and BP of 155/100. No peripheral neuropathy was detected and last eye check-up was normal. A high
                 level of blood sugar was recorded. Additionally, FBE, U&E, creatinine, LFTs, full lipid profile and HbA1c was requested. Atacand
                 was commenced, a follow-up after two weeks were conducted.

                 Six days later, Mrs Sharma presented with the results of the priorly investigations, an elevated levels of HbA1c along with lipid
                 profile were found.

                 On 12/01/2014 visit, Mrs Sharma was counseled to change metformin from 2 tablets at night to 1 tablet twice per day, in addition to
                 Atorvastatin was prescribed.

                 On today’s visit, Mrs Sharma her fasting sugar test was higher than normal parameter.

                 Should you have any queries do not hesitate to contact me.

                 Yours sincerely
                 Doctor
